Question B-002-003-002.

Why the correct answer is right: When answering voice CQ, name the calling station once, say “this is,” and then give your own call sign.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Say the other station's call sign at least five times, followed by \"this is,\" then your call sign twice": Calling the other station at least five times and doubling your call is excessive for a routine answer.
- sourceIndex 2: "Say the other station's call sign at least three times, followed by \"this is,\" and your call sign at least five times": Multiple repetitions of both call signs make the response long and less efficient.
- sourceIndex 3: "Say your call sign twice, followed by \"calling,\" then the other station's call sign": This puts your own call first, so the CQ caller has to wait until the end to know which CQ is being answered.
